Although I have been largely avoiding the absurdity of recent social trends, I want to pass on a bit of wisdom from my background (whole family in STEM, and now over half a decade personally in o-chem).

Scientific studies are almost always misunderstood by the masses (this includes pop-sci news as well) because people don't understand 1) statistics and 2) methodology. Generally, if you can test a phenomena directly (like is common in physics/chem), then there will be no statistics and straightforward methodology. When you can't directly test a phenomena, you must indirectly test it using statistical methods, and methodology necessarily gets more complex. This means that researchers of these studies make use of far more inference and logical steps to reach meaningful conclusions (as compared to the 'harder' disciplines), and each logical step implicitly bakes in another assumption. As a result, even well meaning researchers frequently draw non-sequitur conclusions, let alone errors in sampling and methodology.

 

This beings me to researchers that are not well meaning: always be doubtful of new research, particularly those using statistical methods, in highly politically charged sectors; always read the studies yourself from the standpoint of a peer reviewer. You have to - there are just too many avenues for manipulation of conclusions for those with agendas.

This is why many of us consider physics and chemistry to be the only real sciences. Direct testing is god - no inferences, no games, no manipulation.
